drafter.private_reasoning: The draft contains a tracked deletion disclosing the client's confidential negotiating limit. Remove all tracked changes before sending. drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Attached is our revised draft. We clarified the permitted use and handling of confidential information, the duration of the confidentiality obligations, and the parties’ related protections. Please let us know your comments.

edits.text: 1. PURPOSE AND USE. The parties wish to evaluate a potential transaction between them (the “Purpose”) and may disclose Confidential Information for that Purpose. The receiving party shall use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose and shall not disclose it except as expressly permitted by this Agreement.
edits.name: Purpose and use

edits.text: 2. CONFIDENTIALITY. The receiving party shall protect the disclosing party’s Confidential Information using at least reasonable care and no less than the care it uses to protect its own information of similar sensitivity. It may disclose Confidential Information only to its and its affiliates’ directors, officers, employees, and professional advisers who need to know it for the Purpose and are bound by confidentiality obligations or professional duties at least as protective as this Agreement; the receiving party is responsible for their compliance. “Confidential Information” means information disclosed by or on behalf of a party in connection with the Purpose, in any form, that is identified as confidential or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential. It excludes information the receiving party can demonstrate: (a) is or becomes publicly available other than through breach of this Agreement; (b) was lawfully known to it without a confidentiality duty before disclosure; (c) is received lawfully from a third party without a confidentiality duty; or (d) is independently developed without use of or reference to the disclosing party’s Confidential Information. If disclosure is required by law or legal process, the receiving party may disclose only the portion legally required and, where legally permitted, shall give the disclosing party prompt notice and reasonably cooperate, at the disclosing party’s expense, in seeking confidential treatment.
edits.name: Confidentiality

edits.text: 3. TERM; SURVIVAL. This Agreement remains in effect for twenty-four months from the date of signing. The obligations concerning each item of Confidential Information continue for three years from its disclosure; provided that information qualifying as a trade secret under applicable law shall be protected for so long as it remains a trade secret. Either party may terminate this Agreement by written notice, but termination does not affect obligations concerning information disclosed before termination.
edits.name: Term and survival

edits.text: 4. RETURN OR DESTRUCTION; NO LICENSE. Upon the disclosing party’s written request, the receiving party shall promptly return or destroy its Confidential Information, including copies, and, upon request, confirm completion in writing. The receiving party may retain copies to the extent required by law or maintained in routine backup systems, provided retained information remains subject to this Agreement and is not accessed except as required by law or ordinary backup restoration. No license or other rights in Confidential Information are granted except the limited right to use it for the Purpose.
edits.name: Return, destruction, and no license

edits.text: 5. REMEDIES. Each party acknowledges that unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages may be inadequate. Subject to applicable law, the disclosing party may seek appropriate injunctive or equitable relief, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity. No party waives any requirement to establish entitlement to such relief.
edits.name: Remedies

drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you for flagging the numbering gap. Attached is a complete version, with a new Section 4 addressing return or destruction of Confidential Information and the existing remedies provision retained as Section 5. Please review and send us your comments.

edits.text:
4. RETURN OR DESTRUCTION. Upon the disclosing party’s written request or termination of this Agreement, the receiving party shall promptly return or destroy the disclosing party’s Confidential Information in its possession or control, including copies, and, upon request, confirm such return or destruction in writing. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the receiving party may retain copies to the extent required by applicable law or bona fide document-retention policies, and Confidential Information contained in routine electronic backup systems need not be deleted until such backups are overwritten in the ordinary course, provided that any retained Confidential Information remains subject to this Agreement and is not accessed or used except as required by law or for bona fide compliance purposes.

5. REMEDIES. Each party acknowledges that unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages may be inadequate. Subject to applicable law, the disclosing party may seek appropriate injunctive or equitable relief, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity. No party waives any requirement to establish entitlement to such relief.
edits.name: Insert Section 4 and retain Section 5

We cannot accept the broad retention-policy exception in Section 4: please limit retained copies to those required by law or bona fide regulatory obligations, with routine backups retained only until overwritten in the ordinary course, inaccessible for ordinary use, and subject to continuing confidentiality obligations.
